question: The Commission Representation in Italy launched a call for proposals in February 2025 (COMM/IT/GRANTS/2025) for communication and media actions to foster dialogue in Italy on the role and activities of the European Union, the political priorities of the Commission and the difference that all of the above make to the lives of EU citizens.

However, several irregularities concerning this tender procedure have come to light: all the deadlines have been postponed, while applicants – who had initially been instructed to use the wrong form – have been asked to submit detailed proposals but also to adhere to a 2 500 character limit, a paltry figure. In the light of the above: 1.
How can the Commission justify requiring all applicants to submit three paper copies of their proposals, an arrangement that runs counter to the EU’s sustainability and digital transition objectives?

Does the Commission really believe that it is appropriate for proposals for very important calls for tender to be subject to character limits that are so restrictive that they prevent applicants from providing a full technical description of their projects?
What steps will the Commission take to correct any discrepancies and ensure that all participants are treated fairly?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (13.4.2026) The arrangements for submitting grant applications fall under Article 152 of the Financial Regulation1, which allows for either electronic or paper-based submissions.

Commission services are progressively onboarding electronic submission through the dedicated e-grants system which is expected to become the standard method in the near future, completely phasing out paper submissions. Character limits for calls for proposals are set taking carefully into account the information needed to reply adequately to the award criteria; they are proportionate to the required level of detail.

In this procedure, no proposals were excluded for exceeding these limits, however the information beyond the character limit was not taken into consideration, as announced in the call for proposals. The Commission is committed to ensuring due process, i.e. that all general and procedural principles applicable to grants have been complied with in accordance with Article 191 of the Financial Regulation.

In cases where a correction needs to be made to a call for proposals, the Commission takes all required steps to ensure transparency and equal treatment. Where necessary, applicants are asked to provide clarifications or missing documents. Commission services always perform ex-ante controls where required for grant procedures, ensuring equal and fair treatment of all applicants.
1 Regulation (EU, Euratom) 2024/2509 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 23 September 2024 on
the financial rules applicable to the general budget of the Union (recast), available at http://data.europa.eu/eli/reg/2024/2509/oj.
